summary.title: Scenario 3 - Microservices Healthcare Application
summary.description: A healthcare organisation microservices-based patient management system comprising a Patient Portal, Identity Service, Medical Records Service, Appointment Service, Notification Service, and API Gateway. The patient portal and API gateway are exposed to the public internet while all inter-service communication occurs over an internal network.

data.name: Trust Boundary A: Public Internet
data.description: Separates public internet from DMZ - highest risk boundary

data.name: Trust Boundary B: DMZ
data.description: Separates DMZ from internal services

data.name: Trust Boundary C: Internal Services
data.description: Internal microservices network - inter-service communication

data.name: Third Party: SMS/Email Providers
data.description: External notification service providers

data.name: Patient
data.description: Patient accessing the portal via public internet to view medical records and book appointments

data.name: Patient Portal
data.description: Web frontend exposed to the public internet. Patients access medical records and book appointments through this interface.

threats.title: Cross-Site Scripting on Patient Portal
threats.description: Attacker injects malicious scripts into the patient portal via user inputs. Executes in victims browsers to steal session tokens or patient health data. Affects Patient Portal.
threats.mitigation: Implement strict Content Security Policy (CSP), sanitise all inputs, apply output encoding. Reference OWASP Top 10 A03:2021.

threats.title: Patient Portal DDoS Attack
threats.description: Attacker floods the patient portal with requests rendering it unavailable to legitimate patients. Prevents access to medical records and appointment booking. Affects Patient Portal.
threats.mitigation: Deploy a Web Application Firewall (WAF), implement rate limiting, use a CDN with DDoS protection. Reference NIST 800-53 SC-5.

data.name: API Gateway
data.description: Routes all inbound requests to appropriate backend microservices. Exposed to the public internet.

threats.title: API Gateway DDoS
threats.description: Attacker overwhelms the API Gateway with requests causing service outage across all internal microservices since all traffic routes through it. Affects API Gateway.
threats.mitigation: Implement rate limiting per client, use API gateway throttling policies, deploy behind a load balancer with DDoS mitigation. Reference NIST 800-53 SC-5.

threats.title: Sensitive PHI Exposure via API Response
threats.description: API gateway returns excessive patient health information (PHI) in API responses without field-level filtering, exposing sensitive medical data to unauthorised parties. Affects API Gateway and Medical Records Service.
threats.mitigation: Implement response filtering at the API gateway level. Apply field-level access control. Encrypt all data in transit using TLS 1.3. Reference OWASP Top 10 A02 and HIPAA requirements.

data.name: Identity Service
data.description: Handles authentication and authorisation using OAuth 2.0 and issues JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) to authenticated users

threats.title: JWT Forgery Attack
threats.description: Attacker forges a JWT by exploiting a weak signing secret or the none algorithm vulnerability, creating a token with elevated privileges to access other patients medical records. Affects Identity Service.
threats.mitigation: Use strong asymmetric signing keys (RS256). Validate algorithm header strictly, rejecting none. Implement short token expiry with refresh tokens. Reference OWASP JWT Security Cheat Sheet.

threats.title: Broken OAuth Scope - Privilege Escalation
threats.description: Attacker manipulates OAuth 2.0 scope parameters during the authorisation flow to obtain tokens with broader permissions than intended, gaining access to administrative or other patient records. Affects Identity Service.
threats.mitigation: Strictly validate and enforce OAuth scopes server-side. Never trust client-supplied scope claims. Implement least-privilege token issuance. Reference OWASP Top 10 A01:2021.

threats.title: JWT Not Expiring - Session Persistence Attack
threats.description: JWTs issued without short expiry times remain valid indefinitely. A stolen token can be reused by an attacker long after the legitimate session ended, maintaining unauthorised access to patient data. Affects Identity Service and Medical Records Service.
threats.mitigation: Set short JWT expiry (15 minutes). Implement refresh token rotation. Maintain a token revocation list. Reference NIST 800-53 IA-11.

data.name: Medical Records Service
data.description: Stores and retrieves patient medical records. Verifies JWTs with the Identity Service before serving data.

threats.title: Unauthorised Medical Record Tampering
threats.description: An attacker with a stolen or forged JWT modifies patient medical records including diagnoses, medications, or test results. This could directly harm patient safety. Affects Medical Records Service.
threats.mitigation: Implement record-level integrity checks using cryptographic hashing. Enforce write permissions separately from read permissions. Maintain immutable audit logs. Reference ISO 27001 A.14.1.

threats.title: Audit Log Deletion - Covering Attack Tracks
threats.description: An attacker who has gained access deletes or alters audit logs to remove evidence of their actions such as unauthorised record access or modifications. Affects all services but primarily Medical Records Service.
threats.mitigation: Store audit logs in a write-once, append-only tamper-evident system. Use a separate logging service with restricted delete permissions. Reference NIST 800-53 AU-9.

data.name: Appointment Service
data.description: Manages appointment scheduling. Reads patient data from the Medical Records Service.

threats.title: Inter-Service Data Tampering
threats.description: An attacker on the internal network intercepts and modifies data flows between the Appointment Service and Medical Records Service, altering appointment details or injecting false patient data. Affects Appointment Service and Medical Records Service.
threats.mitigation: Implement mutual TLS (mTLS) for all inter-service communication. Use service mesh with identity verification. Reference NIST 800-53 SC-8.

data.name: Notification Service
data.description: Sends appointment reminders via SMS and email using third-party providers

threats.title: Sensitive Data in Notification Logs
threats.description: The notification service logs full message content including patient names, appointment details, and health information. These logs may be accessible to unauthorised staff or attackers. Affects Notification Service.
threats.mitigation: Implement log redaction to remove PHI from logs. Apply data minimisation principles. Encrypt log storage. Reference HIPAA minimum necessary standard and ISO 27001 A.12.4.

threats.title: Spoofed Notification Service
threats.description: An attacker deploys a rogue notification service on the internal network impersonating the legitimate service to intercept appointment data or send fraudulent SMS and email messages to patients. Affects Notification Service.
threats.mitigation: Implement service-to-service authentication using mutual TLS and service mesh identity. Validate service certificates before accepting connections. Reference NIST 800-53 IA-3.
